Front desk, good evening. This is Grace.
Hi, Grace. This is room 714. I am sorry, but it is very noisy.
Oh, I am sorry. What is the problem?
My neighbors have a party. I couldn't sleep. I could hear the music through the wall.
I understand. Could you wait ten minutes? I can call room 716.
I called them at midnight, but they couldn't hear the phone.
OK. Then I can give you a new room. Room 1102, on the eleventh floor. It is very quiet.
Thank you. And the air conditioning is broken. I couldn't turn it on.
The new room has a new one. Do you need anything else?
Could you send an extra pillow, please?
Of course. A pillow and a blanket to room 1102. Your new key is here at the desk.

The worst night of my trip was in Lisbon. The hotel was beautiful, but my room was next to the elevator. I could hear the elevator all night: up, down, up, down. I couldn't sleep. At two in the morning I called the front desk, but nobody answered. I couldn't find my earplugs, so I put a pillow on my head. Terrible. In the morning I went to the desk and I said: could I have a quiet room, please? And they gave me a room on the top floor, with a view of the river. The second night I could sleep for nine hours.

When I was a child, I couldn't swim, and I was afraid of the sea. My brother could swim very well, and I was so jealous. When I was twenty, I couldn't speak English. I could say hello and thank you, and that was all. Now I can swim, and I swim in the sea every summer. And now I can speak English, not perfectly, but I can travel alone and I can talk to people. My advice? What you couldn't do before, maybe you can do now. You need to try.
